texto:
Community gardens are becoming more popular in many cities around the world. These are pieces of land where a group of people works together to grow fruits, vegetables, and flowers. Usually, these gardens are in empty spaces, like old parking lots or on the rooftops of buildings. Anyone can join, and you don't need to be an expert gardener to participate. It’s a great way to learn new skills.

The benefits of these gardens are numerous. First, they provide fresh, healthy food for the community. People can eat what they grow, which is often cheaper and tastier than store-bought produce. But the advantages are not just about food. They are also great social spaces where neighbors meet and work together. This helps build stronger, friendlier communities.

In addition, community gardens are good for the environment. They help make cities greener and provide a home for bees and butterflies. While they need regular care and volunteers to be successful, they are a wonderful addition to any urban area.

preguntas.pregunta: According to the text, what is a social benefit of community gardens?

opciones.B: They help people sell vegetables to stores.
opciones.C: They allow neighbors to meet and connect.
opciones.D: They are usually located far from the city.

preguntas.explicacion: La respuesta correcta es C porque el texto especifica que los huertos son espacios sociales importantes. Dice explícitamente: 'They are also great social spaces where neighbors meet and work together'. Esto significa que son lugares para que los vecinos se conozcan y colaboren. Las otras opciones son incorrectas: A no se menciona; el texto dice que es una forma de aprender 'to learn new skills', pero no que ofrezcan cursos profesionales. B no está en el texto. D es lo contrario de lo que dice el texto ('in many cities'). E es incorrecta porque el texto compara el producto del huerto favorablemente con el producto comprado en la tienda ('store-bought produce').

preguntas.pregunta: From the text, we can infer that community gardens...

opciones.B: ...are only for people who are expert gardeners.
opciones.C: ...have a positive impact on more than just food supply.
opciones.D: ...are mainly for growing flowers, not food.
opciones.E: ...can replace all supermarkets in a city.

preguntas.explicacion: La respuesta correcta es C. El texto no dice esto directamente, pero podemos inferirlo de toda la información. Describe beneficios más allá de la comida, incluyendo beneficios sociales ('great social spaces where neighbors meet') y ambientales ('good for the environment'). This implies their positive impact is broad and not limited to food. Las otras opciones son incorrectas: A no está respaldada, el texto solo dice que necesitan 'regular care and volunteers'. B es falsa, el texto dice claramente 'you don't need to be an expert gardener'. D es incorrecta, ya que menciona 'fruits, vegetables, and flowers'. E es una exageración que no se puede concluir del texto.
